participants.note: Concept ACKed, but objected to 10 standby sessions as excessive resource usage and raised concerns about startup rate limiting
supported the concept but objected to keeping a bank of 10 standby sessions as wasteful
raised concern that extra sessions expiring after 10 minutes would waste network resources
asked whether the change only applies when inbound I2P connections are disabled

claims.harm: a pool of 10 idle sessions doubles network resource usage and may trigger router tunnel build rate limits at startup
claims.quote: 10 standby sessions is a lot, except maybe at startup. If your I2P connections limit is 10, then you're doubling your network resource usage.
claims.settled_by_quote: reduce the pre-created sessions to 1, given the above.

claims.harm: holding a bank of 10 sessions is wasteful unless demand rate requires it
claims.quote: I'm very concerned about having the session bank be 10 sessions long. ... keeping a bank of 10 of them is pretty wasteful.
claims.settled_by_quote: reduce the pre-created sessions to 1, given the above.

claims.harm: extra sessions expire after 10 minutes and waste resources if not used before expiration
claims.quote: If we don't use these extra sessions before they expire, their creation would be a waste of ressources.
claims.settled_by_quote: reduce the pre-created sessions to 1, given the above.

support.reason: supports decoupling session creation from use for anonymity

result.notes: First read of PR 32065. I2P router developers zzzi2p and eyedeekay and reviewer mzumsande all raised concerns about the overhead of caching up to 10 unused sessions; vasild resolved these concerns by reducing the pre-created session limit to 1.
